assumptions: Objections are founder-supplied text, at most 40 items and 1200 characters per item.
The sample is directional evidence and may not represent the full customer population.
effects: Writes reports/SALES_OBJECTION_BRIEF.md in the bound project.
Makes no external provider writes and sends no messages.
cost_drivers: One bounded Codex procedure run; cost depends on input and project context size.

cases.description: Several objections repeat around value, implementation effort, and trust, so the report should produce clusters and concrete messaging changes.

objections: I do not see enough value to justify the price.
The subscription feels expensive for our current team.
I am worried setup will take too much engineering time.
How long would implementation take for a small team?
We need proof from companies like ours before we buy.
Do you have a case study from a similar company?
inputs.audience: Small product teams evaluating a new B2B software tool
inputs.product_context: The product is a B2B software subscription sold to small teams.

cases.description: The sample contains different buying concerns and should not be presented as one universal problem.

objections: I need approval from my manager.
The price is higher than expected.
Can it integrate with our existing workflow?

cases.description: Three generic statements do not provide three useful objections, so the workflow should state that the evidence is insufficient rather than inventing a pattern.
